small_guidance: Switch the scatter strategy: instead of one program per input voxel doing atomic_adds across OC tiles (which serializes via L2 atomics and inflates DRAM traffic), keep the same kernel shape but increase BLOCK_OC to 64 and add an autotune over (BLOCK_OC, BLOCK_IC, num_warps) ∈ {(32,16,4),(64,16,4),(64,32,8),(32,32,4)}; also drop the bias-expand initialization (which writes the full output once before any atomic_add) and instead pass bias into a fused epilogue or zero-init and add bias in the BN kernel.
large_guidance: Redesign as a gather-based im2col GEMM: one program per (N, OC tile, output-spatial tile), where each thread computes a complete output element by looping over (ic, kd, kh, kw) and gathering the corresponding input voxel (only when (od+PD-kd) is divisible by SD and the implied iD/iH/iW is in-range). This eliminates atomic_adds entirely, materializes each output once, and turns the workload into a dense fp32 GEMM of shape (OC) x (IC*KD*KH*KW) per output tile. Fold BN scale/shift and the per-sample spatial-mean subtraction into the epilogue: do a two-pass kernel where pass 1 writes y=scale*conv+shift and accumulates per-(N,C) sum, pass 2 subtracts the mean — or, since OD*OH*OW≈35k, keep BN-fold in the conv epilogue and run a separate small mean-subtract kernel. Use channels_last-style layout (OC contiguous) with BLOCK_M=32-64 OC, BLOCK_N=64-128 spatial, BLOCK_K=16-32 over IC*KD*KH*KW, num_warps=4, num_stages=2, sized to fit ~80KB SMEM.
